subject: Post-demo data lifecycle clarification and custody asks
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@tridata.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Gonzales <maya@tridata.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — a few data questions

Marissa — thanks again for the walkthrough today. Two quick follow-ups from our security team while we finish internal scoring: what exactly gets persisted from a typical prompt/response cycle, and where does that data live?

High-level asks they sent over:
- Which elements of a prompt or generated output are written to long-term storage vs ephemeral caches?
- Where are any persisted artifacts located geographically (region/zone)?
- Retention windows and whether TTLs are configurable per customer/route.
- Access controls and whether customer-managed KMS can be used for stored artifacts.

We also attached the telemetry matrix they requested (attached). If you can map the answers to the rows in the spreadsheet that'd be super helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of Platform Security
TriData
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@tridata.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Maya Gonzales <maya@tridata.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — a few data questions

Alex — great questions, and good to see the matrix. I started a short mapping below; Rishi is copying in the implementation detail and Stephanie will handle the compliance artifacts (SOC2, DPIA notes).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Ephemeral: session-level prompt text and generated tokens live in runtime memory and KV cache with a default TTL of 1 hour.
- Short-term persistence: request traces and minimal metadata (request id, model id, token counts, client route) retained for 30 days by default for troubleshooting and billing. No prompt text is stored by default in this bucket for customers on our Standard plan.
- Long-term optional persistence: customers can elect to persist prompts and outputs for audit/analytics; when enabled, data is written to encrypted object storage in the selected region with a customer-configurable TTL (30/90/365 days) and optional customer-managed KMS.

Action items for clarity:
1) Rishi — can you confirm the KV cache behavior with regards to partial long prompts and how we log cache hits/misses?
2) Stephanie — please attach the excerpt from the DPIA that maps to the optional persistence path and note any SLAs around deletion.
3) Alex/Maya — if you have a preferred region and TTL, let us know and we'll include it in the config sample.

Attachments: tri-demo-telemetry-matrix.xlsx (we saw it)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Park <alex.park@tridata.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Maya Gonzales <maya@tridata.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — a few data questions

Alex — following up on Marissa's summary with the technical specifics you asked for and how they map to the telemetry matrix rows:

1) Runtime memory & KV cache:
- What: ephemeral token buffers and KV cache (attention/key-value caches used for session continuation).
- Where: resides on serving nodes in the region of the inference endpoint (not written to object storage).
- Retention: default TTL is 1 hour; cache eviction policies apply. These are not included in logs or long-term storage.
- PII risk: transient; we recommend masking high-risk fields client-side before sending in prompts if you require absolute non-persistence.

2) Request traces / observability logs:
- What: trace id, timestamps, latency, model variant, token counts, error codes.
- Where: central logging cluster in the chosen region; text fields are redacted by default for Standard customers.
- Retention: 30 days standard; 90/365-day options for Enterprise.
- Access: role-based access via Redwood Console; audit logs available to customers with Private deployment.

3) Optional persisted artifacts (prompts & outputs) — customer opt-in path:
- Storage: encrypted object store in customer-selected region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 supported).
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, option to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM (supported for Dedicated/Private only).
- TTL: configurable per-customer/route; defaults: 30/90/365 days. Immediate deletion API available for compliance requests.
- Deletion guarantees: garbage-collection process runs within 24–72 hours after TTL expiry; for BYOK customers deletion includes key revocation steps per contract.

4) Audit & exports:
- We can provide time-bounded exports (S3-compatible export with temp credentials) and documented deletion receipts for audits.

If it helps, I can produce a small config snippet showing the flags to turn on persistence and BYOK.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Gonzales <maya@tridata.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@tridata.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — a few data questions

Thanks Marissa and Rishi — this is very helpful and maps cleanly to our matrix. A couple of clarification asks before we move to a short pilot: 

- For the optional persisted artifacts path, can you confirm whether user identifiers are stored alongside prompts by default, or whether we can store prompts in a de-identified blob linked only by an internal request id? We prefer de-identified storage if possible.
- If we enable BYOK, can Redwood confirm the deletion receipt process includes key destruction confirmation? Our compliance team needs a deterministic proof of deletion.

We'll review and pick a pilot TTL (likely 90 days) and preferred region (us-west-2) and come back with a doc by EOD Wednesday. If you can provide the config snippet Rishi mentioned and a sample deletion receipt template that would be great.

Thanks — Maya
Director, Security & Compliance
TriData
